facts.statement: The genus Palatodonta was first described by James M. Neenan, Nicole Klein, and Torsten M. Scheyer in 2013.
facts.quote: Palatodonta was first named by James M. Neenan, Nicole Klein and Torsten M. Scheyer in 2013

facts.statement: The type species was discovered by amateur paleontologist Remco Bleeker in the summer of 2010 at the Silbeco quarry near Winterswijk.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Remco Bleeker, an amateur paleontologist, who discovered the fossil in the summer of 2010 at the Silbeco quarry near Winterswijk.

facts.statement: The only known fossil is a well-preserved skull of a juvenile individual designated as holotype TW480000470.
facts.quote: Palatodonta is known from the holotype TW480000470, a well-preserved skull of a juvenile individual.

facts.statement: Palatodonta lived during the early Middle Triassic (early Anisian stage) in the Netherlands.
facts.quote: Palatodonta is an extinct genus of neodiapsid reptile known from the early Middle Triassic (early Anisian stage) of the Netherlands.

facts.statement: In 2013, Palatodonta was classified as a basal placodontiform related to the marine reptile group known as placodonts.
facts.quote: It was initially described in 2013 as a basal placodontiform closely related to a group of marine reptiles called placodonts

facts.statement: A 2023 study reclassified Palatodonta as a sauropterygomorph and the sister taxon to Eusaurosphargis.
facts.quote: A 2023 study instead classified it as a sauropterygomorph and the sister taxon to Eusaurosphargis.

facts.statement: Palatodonta possessed a tall skull with a short, blunt snout.
facts.quote: The skull is tall and has a short, blunt snout.

facts.statement: The premaxillae bore four large, chisel-shaped teeth that leaned forward, similar to those of many placodonts.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla has four large and chisel-shaped teeth which are slightly procumbent (leaning forwards), similar to many placodonts.

facts.statement: Palatodonta had a single row of large teeth on the palatine bone running parallel to the maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: The palatine bone, which lies along the palate (roof of the mouth) parallel to the maxilla, hosted a single row of large teeth similar to those of the maxilla.

facts.statement: The lower jaw contained at least 14 sharp, narrow teeth that became larger and more robust toward the rear.
facts.quote: The dentary has at least 14 pointed teeth which are sharp and narrow, though they become larger and more robust further back in the jaw.

facts.statement: Palatodonta had a very large, circular eye socket.
facts.quote: The orbit (eye socket) was very large and circular.

facts.statement: The postorbital bridge was positioned low on the skull, exposing both temporal openings from the side.
facts.quote: The postorbital bridge is set relatively low on the skull, so that both temporal openings are well-exposed from the side.

facts.statement: Unlike the thick, blunt palatal teeth of placodonts, Palatodonta possessed thin, pointed palatal teeth resembling those of other reptiles.
facts.quote: Like placodonts, it has a row of large teeth on its palate, but while these teeth are thick and blunt in placodonts, Palatodonta has palatal teeth that are thin and pointed (like the teeth that line the jaws of most other reptiles).

facts.statement: Researchers once interpreted Palatodonta as a transitional form between placodonts and less specialized reptiles.
facts.quote: Under this interpretation, Palatodonta is transitional between placodonts and less specialized reptiles.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Palatodonta belongs within Sauropterygia; a 2023 study places it as a sauropterygomorph sister to Eusaurosphargis, close to but outside the group.
facts.quote: A 2023 study instead classified it as a sauropterygomorph and the sister taxon to Eusaurosphargis. In other words, it is close to, but not within, Sauropterygia (the group containing placodonts and other marine reptiles such as nothosaurs and plesiosaurs).

rejected.statement: Palatodonta featured a large, boomerang-shaped jugal bone that excluded the maxilla from the orbit's rim.
rejected.quote: This 'boomerang-shaped' jugal is similar in shape to that of Paraplacodus; unlike Paraplacodus, it is large enough to exclude the maxilla from the rim of the orbit.
